{{Short description|American computer scientist and cryptographer}}

{{BLP primary sources|date=June 2021}}{{Infobox person
| name               = Kevin McCurley
| education          = [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]

'''Kevin Snow McCurley'''<ref name="phd" /> is a [[mathematician]], [[computer scientist]], and [[cryptographer]], and a former<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kevin McCurley|url=https://mccurley.org/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816141456/http://www.mccurley.org/|archive-date=16 August 2021|access-date=12 June 2021|website=mccurley.org}}</ref>{{Unreliable source?|date=June 2021}} [[research scientist]] at [[Google]]. He has written publications about [[information retrieval]], [[algorithm]]s, [[parallel computing]], [[cryptography]], and [[number theory]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=3 December 2009|title=An Interview with Google's Kevin McCurley {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|url=https://www.maa.org/news/interview-googles-kevin-mccurley|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151017190350/https://www.maa.org/news/interview-googles-kevin-mccurley|archive-date=17 October 2015|access-date=3 June 2021|website=www.maa.org}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
When he was a child, McCurley had built model planes and cars, and he enjoyed making things with his hands.<ref name=":0" />

McCurley attended a high school in [[San Jose, California]]. There, one of his teachers, Judy Jones, showed him that "mathematics really could be fun and interesting" and encouraged him to attend mathematical contests.<ref name=":0" />

In his first year at [[Santa Clara University]], McCurley had Jerry Anderson, a former president of the MAA, as his professor in calculus; Anderson told "interesting stories" and was able to "relate the mathematics to history and to activities that were meaningful".<ref name=":0" /> He started out as a mathematician, but he later retrained himself as a computer scientist.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=McCurley|first=Kevin|title=Kevin McCurley|url=http://pages.swcp.com/~mccurley/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081225144042/http://pages.swcp.com/~mccurley/|archive-date=25 December 2008|access-date=2 December 2021|website=pages.swcp.com}}</ref>

In 1981, McCurley received his [[Ph.D.]] in [[mathematics]] from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]].<ref name="phd">{{MathGenealogy|id=3992}}</ref> His dissertation in [[analytic number theory]] was titled ''Explicit Estimates for Functions of Primes in Arithmetic Progressions'', and his advisor was Paul Trevier Bateman.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="phd" /> He also received a master's in statistics there.<ref name=":0" />

In the fall of 1995, McCurley taught an undergraduate course on cryptology at the [[University of New Mexico]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Modern Cryptology Links|url=http://www-math.ucdenver.edu/~wcherowi/courses/m5410/ctclinks.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100704090518/http://www-math.ucdenver.edu/~wcherowi/courses/m5410/ctclinks.html|archive-date=4 July 2010|access-date=3 June 2021|website=www-math.ucdenver.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=CS 431 - Cryptology in Computing|url=http://pages.swcp.com/~mccurley/course/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090324170718/http://pages.swcp.com/~mccurley/course/|archive-date=24 March 2009|access-date=3 June 2021|website=pages.swcp.com}}</ref>{{Better source needed|date=December 2021}}

After he was a post-doc at [[Michigan State University]], McCurley took a job at [[USC (Los Angeles)]], where he published some papers with [[Leonard Adleman]] about algorithms and complexity.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Before 2005{{When|date=June 2021}}, McCurley worked at IBM Almaden Research Center, Sandia National Laboratories, and at the University of Southern California''.''<ref name=":0" /> McCurley worked in a cryptography group at [[Sandia National Laboratories]], where he worked on applying number theory to cryptography and parallel computing.<ref name=":0" /> He then worked at IBM Research in California{{When|date=December 2021}} on [[digital rights management]], where he wrote a few patents;<ref name=":0" /> he was there in January 1999.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mills|first=Elinor|date=January 21, 1999|title=CNN - Congress considers easing cryptography rules|url=http://www.cnn.com/TECH/computing/9901/21/crypto.idg/index.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000423000011/http://www.cnn.com/TECH/computing/9901/21/crypto.idg/index.html|archive-date=23 April 2000|access-date=3 June 2021|website=www.cnn.com}}</ref>

A former [[president (corporate title)|president]] of the [[International Association for Cryptologic Research]], McCurley was selected as an IACR Fellow in 2005 for his "exemplary service as IACR President and essential leadership in IACR information systems".<ref name="fellow">{{cite web|date=|title=IACR Fellow citation|url=https://www.iacr.org/fellows/2005/McCurley.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060620153559/https://www.iacr.org/fellows/2005/McCurley.html|archive-date=20 June 2006|access-date=2013-01-31|publisher=Iacr.org}}</ref>

From 2005 to at least 2009{{When|date=June 2021}} McCurley was a research scientist at Google Research.<ref name=":0" /> There, he worked on search, advertisements, and [[Android (operating system)|Android]].<ref name=":0" />

== Miscellany ==
In 2000, McCurley suggested, while speaking at Financial Cryptography '00 conference, that, as a countermeasure against [[email spam]], recipients of email from unknown senders should request that the message include a first name, a few dollars, or a donation to a specific charity as compensation. He also suggested that this be formalized in an [[open standard]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|date=23 February 2000|title=Send Out Spam, Pay the Bill|language=en-US|magazine=Wired|url=https://www.wired.com/2000/02/send-out-spam-pay-the-bill/|access-date=3 June 2021|issn=1059-1028}}</ref>

=== Bets about P vs NP ===
McCurley has made three bets with Ron Fagin about the outcome of the [[P versus NP problem]]. In each bet, the outcome P = NP would require Fagin to pay McCurley $50, whereas P != NP would require McCurley to pay Fagin $10. The first bet had a deadline of 31 December 2010, the second a deadline of 31 December 2020, and the third (made in 2021) a deadline of 31 December 2030.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wanna bet on P=NP?|url=http://pages.swcp.com/~mccurley/bet.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629144709/http://pages.swcp.com/~mccurley/bet.html|archive-date=29 June 2020|access-date=3 June 2021|website=pages.swcp.com}}</ref>{{Update after|2030|12|31}}
